text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish TVN company, controlled by the ITI Neovision media group, and the U.S.'s CME Media Enterprises B have acquired a 49-percent stake in the Televizja Wisla regional television broadcasting company.

- Poland's railway monopolist PKP is likely this month to contract electric engines worth up to $200 million from Adtranz, the railway joint venture of ABB and Daimler Benz, PKP president Jan Janik said.
In the next five years PKP will spend 8 billion zlotys on rolling stock modernisation.

- The Nafta Polska SA petroleum holding will carry out the state industrial policy in the oil sector and act as the owner of the holding's member firms until the year 2000, a company strategy document said.

- The United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) will organise several international events in 1997 to attract foreign investment to Poland, UNIDO Polish branch director Krzysztof Loth said.

- More than 3,000 new institutions in the public sector and almost 19,000 new private firms were registered in the first nine months of 1996, showing significant growth compared with results in the same period last year.
NOWA EUROPA
- State-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank expects its 1996 gross profit to reach 420 million zlotys.
- The Warsaw bourse has contracted Coopers & Lybrand to assist in choosing a software firm to introduce new programming for the bourse's computer system.
- Around 45 percent of Poles think that present government economic policy does not allow for improving the economy while 39 percent think it does, a recent survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
- Almost 20 percent of all examined non-alcoholic low-price beverages were withheld by Poland's sanitary inspection body for abusing health ministry regulations.
- Poland-Luxembourg trade turnover in 1995 was at $29.2 million. Polish exports amounted to $8.7 million and imports $20.5 million.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The number of Poland's smallhold farms decreases by up to 25,000 annually, agricultural economy institute researcher Adam Wos said.
- Over 90 Polish and foreign companies will participate in the Women's consumer goods fair to take place in Olsztyn, northeastern Poland, from November 10 to 11.
- The Petrochemia Plock refinery heads the list of Poland's 500 biggest companies published recently by the weekly Nowe Zycie Gospodarcze.
- The Ursus agricultural tractor maker produced 12,033 tractors in the first nine month of this year, showing a decrease in output compared with last year's results in the same period.
ZYCIE
- The number of Poland's telephone subscribers grew by 25 percent in the third quarter of this year compared with last year's results in the same period, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
